html:
The Panará are a Jê-speaking people of the southern Amazon, in northern Mato Grosso and southern Pará in Brazil. Outsiders long called them Kreen-Akrore, and they were feared as giants of the forest. They are thought to descend from the Southern Kayapó, who once lived much further south.

They were contacted in 1973 by the Villas-Bôas brothers, as the military government built the Cuiabá to Santarém highway through their land. Disease killed most of them within two years. In 1975 the 79 survivors were flown to the Xingu Indigenous Park, where they lived among other peoples. In the 1990s they returned to part of their old forest, which had escaped the loggers, and in 2000 a Brazilian court ordered the state to pay them damages, a first for an Indigenous people in Brazil.
